photo.alt: Nôsemanicôs / LADYBUG trail sign showing a red ladybug with black head and black spots, with white Plains Cree syllabics carved across the wing case
photo.caption: 3D printed plaque: red ladybug with black head, black spots, and the syllabics ᓅᓭᒪᓂᒎᐢ in white across its wing case.

linguistics.meaning: Ladybug — literally ‘the female little bug’ (the female-of-the-bug, with maternal/feminine reading)

morphemes.gloss: female-marker prefix: ‘female, mother, dam.’ The same productive prefix that builds nôsemostos ‘cow (female buffalo / cow-bovine),’ nôsepiscâcâs ‘mother bird, hen,’ nôsemâcêsis ‘doe, female deer.’ Marks the specifically-female of any animate species.

NA noun (animate): ‘small bug, little insect, creepy-crawly.’ Itself a diminutive in form (older long-vowel ‑ôs final), grouping with a wide family of animate-small-creature words. The free-standing word for an unspecified small bug.

relatedForms.english: Bug, small insect (the bare noun, either sex)

morphemes.gloss: NA noun: ‘bug, small insect.’ The base from which nôsemanicôs ‘ladybug = female-bug’ is built.

relatedForms.note: The unmarked species-word. Inside nôsemanicôs, the nôse‑ prefix narrows it to the female form.

morphemes.gloss: NA animate plural ending — same ‑ak as in iskwêwak ‘women,’ kahkakiwak ‘ravens,’ mahihkanak ‘wolves.’

relatedForms.note: Animate plural. A swarm of ladybugs would be nôsemanicôsak — same ‑ak ending stacked onto the female-bug headword.
Structural minimal pair: same nôse‑ prefix slotting onto a different animal noun. Shows that the female-marker is fully productive, not specific to bugs.

quickReference.note: Headword on the plaque. NA noun (animate). Some communities also use mîniskos regionally.
Bare noun. Source of the second half of the headword.

quickReference.english: Female-marker prefix (used to derive any female-of-species noun)

quickReference.note: Same nôse‑ prefix on a different animal stem.

culturalStory.heading: About nôsemanicôs — the Female Little Bug
body: Across the prairies the ladybug carries an old reading as a small, marked, distinctly-female creature: brilliant red wing case, black head, polka-dot pattern that reads at any distance, and a habit of clustering on grass-stems where children can pick them up. The Cree name nôsemanicôs takes that reading literally — ‘female (nôse‑) little bug (manicôs).’ The same nôse‑ prefix that builds nôsemostos ‘cow’ (female buffalo) and nôsemâcêsis ‘doe’ shows up here on a tiny scale, marking the ladybug as the female-of-the-bug-family the way the cow is the female-of-the-bovine-family.

The plaque leans into that reading visually: a single red ladybug fills almost the whole white plaque, head turned, six legs splayed for balance, with the syllabics ᓅᓭᒪᓂᒎᐢ picked out in white across the polished red wing case so the language sits inside the body of the animal it names. White on red in 3D-printed PLA is the closest thing to red enamel paint with a dot of white pigment — exactly the colour scheme of the bug itself.

The trail of this name sits on ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐤ ᐊᐢᑭᕀ Nêhiyaw‑Askiy (Plains Cree territory) in the Edmonton river-valley network. Putting the diminutive feminine bug-word back onto an MTB sign places a Plains Cree linguistic micro-pattern (the productive nôse‑ prefix) onto a piece of the everyday landscape — small, polka-dotted, and easy to remember once you see how it is built.

notes: PHYSICAL SIGN OVERRIDES CATALOGUE (syllabics): The plaque is carved with SRO 'nôsemanicôs' (catalogue creeName 'nôsemanicôs' already matches — keep) but the catalogue creeSyllabics is 'ᓄᓭᒪᓂᒑᐢ' which decodes as 'nosemanicâs' (short-o on the first glyph; long-â vowel on the c-glyph ᒑ where the SRO calls for long-ô on c). The plaque-correct syllabics for 'nôsemanicôs' are 'ᓅᓭᒪᓂᒎᐢ' — long-ô glyph ᓅ on the first position (nô) and long-ô glyph ᒎ on the c-position (cô), with the final ᐢ marking the bare ‑s. Coordinator should update catalogue creeSyllabics from 'ᓄᓭᒪᓂᒑᐢ' to 'ᓅᓭᒪᓂᒎᐢ' to match the SRO and the carved plaque.

Morpheme split: 'nôse-manicôs' is a transparent noun-noun compound (female-prefix + bug). Some references treat nôse‑ as a free particle/adjectival rather than a bound prefix; either reading is defensible. The 2-morpheme split surfaces both pieces cleanly for the renderer's hover-pairing.

The third related form (nôsemostos ‘cow / female buffalo’) is provided as a structural minimal pair to expose the productive nôse‑ prefix; readers can then recognise the same prefix on nôsemâcêsis ‘doe’ and other female-of-species words.

Trailforks pick: NO confident match. A direct search for 'Ladybug' in the Edmonton-area Trailforks network returned no hits across three queries. The trail may be unmapped on Trailforks, or be a community/builder name not yet listed. Leaving trailforks: {} and flagging here for a single human-rider Trailforks lookup.

Mapping syllabic ᒎ (CANS U+128E COO) for the 'cô' position assumes the Plains Cree convention where long ô after c is written ᒎ. Some materials use ᒍ (CO, short) with an external long-vowel mark; either is readable but the long-vowel glyph matches the SRO circumflex more transparently.
